   - Once the card is blocked, check recent transactions and note anything you don’t recognize.  
   - The bank will typically open a **fraud claim** for those charges and send you a new card with a new number.

4. **If you can’t reach the bank right now:**  
   - Call **Visa Global Customer Assistance** (if this is a Visa-branded card) from your region; they can help block the card and connect you to the issuer. The number is on Visa’s official site under “Emergency Assistance.”

After you’ve contacted the issuer and had the card blocked, I can help you with:
- Drafting notes for a **fraud/dispute claim** for any unauthorized transactions.
- A checklist of places to update your card on file (subscriptions, digital wallets, etc.).

<action type="say">
Here’s the fastest way to handle this and the wording you can use.

1) How to reach them fastest
- Go to the other bank’s **official website or app**.
- Look for **“Contact us” → “Lost or stolen card”**, or a **24/7 fraud/emergency** number.  
- If there’s a **phone option inside their mobile app**, use that: it often skips menus and verifies you automatically.

Have ready:
- Your **full name**, **DOB**, **address**, and last 4 of SSN (or whatever they usually use to verify you).
- Approx. **time you last had the card** and **when you noticed it missing**.

2) Script to block card + get replacement (say this up front)
You can literally read this:

> “Hi, my name is [your name]. I need to **report my credit card as stolen** and have it **blocked immediately**.  
> I also need you to **order a replacement card right away with rush delivery if possible**.  
> I’ve noticed possible fraudulent activity and I want to **dispute any unauthorized charges and have the account flagged for fraud**.”

If they start verification questions, answer those; then continue with:

> “Please **confirm for me now** that this card is **completely blocked** and **cannot be used anymore**, including for **in‑person, online, or recurring transactions**.”

3) Script to handle fraud charges
After the block is confirmed, say:

> “I’d like to **review recent transactions** on this card and **dispute anything that’s not mine** as fraud.  
> Please **open a fraud claim** for those transactions and **reissue my card with a new number**.”

When you see any charge you didn’t authorize, use:

> “I do **not recognize this transaction** and did **not authorize it**. The card was stolen.  
> Please **mark this as fraud**, **reverse or provisionally credit** the charge, and **include it in the fraud report**.”

Then ask for specifics:

> “Can you tell me:
> 1) **My fraud case or reference number**,  
> 2) When I can expect **a provisional credit or final decision**, and  
> 3) When my **replacement card** will arrive and whether you can **expedite shipping**?”

4) Things to insist on (short checklist)
- Card is **blocked immediately** (not just “monitored”).
- **New card number** (not reusing the old number).
- A **case number** for fraud.
- **Provisional credit** while they investigate, if applicable.

If you tell me which country you’re in, I can tailor this a bit more to your local protections and typical timelines.</action>

<action type="say">
“Hi, my name is [your name]. I’m calling to **report my credit card as stolen**, have it **blocked immediately**, and **order a replacement card with rush delivery**.  

The card is a [Bank Name] Visa. I’m the primary cardholder. I last had the card around [time/date], and I just discovered it’s missing and definitely stolen, not misplaced.

Before we go further, I want to confirm:
1) You will **immediately block this card and stop all new charges**, including in‑person, online, and recurring.  
2) You will **issue a replacement card with a new number** and **rush‑ship it** to my address on file.”

[AFTER VERIFICATION / IF THEY TRY TO ONLY “MONITOR” THE CARD]

“If there’s any option to only ‘monitor’ or keep the card partially active, I **do not consent to that**.  
The card is **stolen**, and I need it **fully blocked and unusable right now**.  
Please confirm it is **completely blocked** and no further transactions can go through.”

[IF THEY RESIST RUSH SHIPPING]

“I understand standard shipping is an option, but because this is a **stolen card and potential fraud situation**, I need you to **escalate this** and **rush‑ship the replacement**.  

If there is any **expedited replacement or emergency card program**, I’d like to use that.  
Please check with a **supervisor or your fraud/emergency department** for the fastest possible replacement and note in my file that I requested expedited handling due to theft and fraud.”

[IF THERE ARE ALREADY 2–3 FRAUD CHARGES]

“I also see **2–3 charges I did not authorize**. I did **not** make these transactions, I did **not** give my card to anyone, and I did **not** give permission for these charges. The card was stolen.

I want to **dispute these as fraud** and have them **included in a fraud claim**.  
Please:
1) **Open a fraud or dispute case** on my account,  
2) **Mark these charges as unauthorized fraud**, and  
3) **Provide provisional credits** while you investigate, if applicable.

Can you please read back the list of recent transactions so I can confirm which ones are mine and which are not?”

[AFTER REVIEWING CHARGES]

“For each transaction I do not recognize, please note:  
‘I did not authorize this transaction. My card was stolen. Mark this as fraud and include it in the fraud investigation.’”

[TO WRAP UP THE CALL]

“Before we end, I want to confirm the following:

1) The **stolen card is fully blocked** and cannot be used anymore.  
2) A **replacement card with a new number** has been ordered and **rush‑shipped**.  
   - What is the **expected delivery date**?  
3) A **fraud/dispute case has been opened** for the unauthorized transactions.  
   - What is my **case or reference number**?  
   - When can I expect **provisional credits or a decision** on those charges?

Please add notes to my account that I reported the card as **stolen** today, [today’s date], and reported these specific transactions as **fraud**.”

[IF THEY PUSH BACK ON ANY POINT]

“For the record, I’m **formally requesting**:
- **Immediate full block** of the stolen card,  
- **Replacement card with a new number**, and  
- **Fraud investigation and disputes** for all unauthorized charges.

If there’s any limitation you can’t change, please **document my request and your response in the account notes**, and let me know how I can **escalate** this or speak with **a supervisor or the fraud department**.”</action>
